title: Single-shot magic state factories for quantum LDPC codes
authors: Varun Menon, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Andrei C. Diaconu, Daniel Bochen Tan, Xiao Xiao, Michael J. Gullans, Qian Xu, Hengyun Zhou, Mikhail D. Lukin, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides
abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes can substantially reduce the qubit overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computation, but any useful architecture based on such codes also requires an efficient mechanism to implement non-Clifford gates in a fault-tolerant manner. We introduce a space-time-efficient magic state factory for high-rate qLDPC codes by combining the transversal non-Clifford gates of recently developed tricycle codes with single-shot four-dimensional balanced product quadcycle codes. The key ingredient is an efficient "escape" mechanism that teleports postselected logical magic states from tricycle codes to larger distance quadcycle codes. Under a standard circuit-level noise model at physical error rate $10^{-3}$, our factories produce $\mathrm{CCZ}$ states at logical error rates as low as $10^{-9}$ with 10-40 times lower space-time cost than state-of-the-art magic state generation methods. The resulting states are directly encoded in high-rate blocks suitable for computation. We identify the quadcycle codes by an AI-assisted search and show that they can serve as excellent memories capable of single-shot error correction. Finally, we present a concrete implementation of the entire factory with highly efficient atom transport on reconfigurable neutral-atom quantum computers. Together, these results provide an end-to-end, practical protocol for producing and utilizing high-fidelity magic states within a high-rate qLDPC architecture, with the lowest space-time cost to date.
summary: This paper presents a novel, highly efficient 'magic state factory' designed for fault-tolerant quantum computation using quantum LDPC codes. It merges tricycle and quadcycle codes via a teleportation mechanism to generate high-fidelity magic states. The protocol is demonstrated on neutral-atom quantum computers, offering a practical, low-overhead pathway to scaling quantum computation.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing a space-time-efficient method to generate high-fidelity magic states required for fault-tolerant quantum computation using quantum LDPC codes.
main_result: The authors propose a factory combining tricycle and quadcycle codes that achieves logical error rates as low as $10^{-9}$ with 10-40 times lower space-time cost than existing methods.
method: The approach uses an 'escape' mechanism to teleport postselected logical magic states from tricycle codes to more robust quadcycle codes via a depth-1 homomorphic CNOT.
model_or_system: The protocol is demonstrated on reconfigurable neutral-atom quantum computers, utilizing the algebraic structure of tricycle and quadcycle codes for state preparation and error correction.
key_observables: Logical error rate (achieving $10^{-9}$), space-time cost (showing 10-40x improvement), and fidelity of generated CCZ states.
important_parameters: Physical error rate ($p = 10^{-3}$), code distances ($d_{3D}$), and the number of available atoms/AODs.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a standard circuit-level noise model at $p = 10^{-3}$, and the efficiency relies on the shared algebraic structure between the two code types.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the 'Transversal dimension-jump magic state factory' process, showing the flow from tricycle to quadcycle blocks, and detail the single-shot error correction capabilities of the quadcycle codes.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the need for efficient magic state generation for qLDPC codes. It then details the combination of tricycle and quadcycle codes, the teleportation mechanism, and finally presents a concrete, end-to-end implementation using neutral atoms.
why_interesting: The integration of advanced quantum error-correcting codes (qLDPC) with a physical implementation platform (neutral atoms) to solve a fundamental resource bottleneck (magic state generation) is highly relevant for experimental quantum computing.

Logical error rate per cycle per logical qubit versus physical error rate p for the [[54, 6, 6]], [[72, 6, 8]], and [[162, 6, 14]] quadcycle codes, from windowed memory simulations under circuit-level depolarizing noise. Post-selected logical error rate per output logical qubit (top) and single-block acceptance fraction (bottom) for the 2 × [[27, 3, 3]] →[[54, 6, 6]] and 2 × [[36, 3, 4]] →[[72, 6, 8]] fac- tories, as a function of the CCZ error rate pCCZ, with all other operations held at depolarizing noise p = 10−3. The simulated CCZ noise is the single-qubit marginal of a three-qubit depo- larizing channel; this marginal is exact because each qubit participates in only one gate in the depth-1 transversal CCZ circuit.
